paper.abstract_en: Conventional analytical models of intrabeam scattering (IBS), such as the Piwinski model and Bjorken-Mtingwa model, generally rely on the assumption of a Gaussian beam distribution, limiting their applicability to non-Gaussian cases. In this work, we develop a multi-Gaussian model to extend analytical IBS calculations to a broader class of non-Gaussian phase-space distributions. The proposed approach represents a non-Gaussian distribution as a superposition of Gaussian components sharing a common covariance matrix but having different mean values. We derived a generalized model for evaluating the momentum second-moment evolution rate and the IBS growth rate. Furthermore, for equally spaced Gaussian components, we developed an infinite bunch train model and introduce a practical truncation rule to reduce computational costs. The model is applied to a representative steady-state microbunching (SSMB) storage ring, where longitudinal overlap between neighboring microbunches is shown to enhance IBS growth rates in all three directions. The proposed framework provides a practical approach to evaluating IBS in non-Gaussian beam distributions and offers a basis for further development toward a more general non-Gaussian IBS theory.
